title: Wave Speed and Doppler Effect Formula

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Waves

expression: v = fλ  ;  Doppler (sound): f' = f × (v ± vo)/(v ∓ vs)
explanation: Basic wave speed relates frequency and wavelength: v = fλ. For the Doppler effect in sound, the apparent frequency f' depends on the relative motion of source and observer with respect to the medium: use + in the numerator when the observer moves TOWARD the source (and − when moving away), and − in the denominator when the source moves TOWARD the observer (and + when moving away) — approaching motion always tends to raise apparent frequency, receding motion lowers it.

variables.meaning: Speed of the wave in the medium
Speed of observer and source relative to the medium

workedExample.scenario: A stationary observer hears an ambulance (source) approaching at 30 m/s, siren frequency 500 Hz, speed of sound 340 m/s.
workedExample.result: f' ≈ 548.4 Hz (higher pitch heard as it approaches)

commonMistakes: Mixing up the sign convention — approaching motion should always raise the apparent frequency; if a calculation gives a lower frequency for an approaching source, a sign has been applied backwards.
Using the source's speed formula for the observer's motion or vice versa — they enter the equation in different places (numerator vs denominator) with different sign rules.
genZNote: Doppler sign convention: approaching always bumps the pitch up, receding always brings it down — no exceptions.
